title: Quantum computation of energy level degeneracy and thermodynamical properties of spin systems
authors: V. M. Tkachuk, M. I. Samar
abstract: We propose a hybrid quantum-classical method for reconstructing energy-level degeneracies and thermodynamic properties of spin systems. A single ancilla qubit is used to measure the partition function at imaginary inverse temperatures. For spectra lying on a known equally spaced energy grid, the inverse discrete Fourier transform allows exact reconstruction of degeneracies in the absence of noise, without spectral leakage. The quantum circuits are optimized using commuting interactions and Eulerian ordering. We demonstrate the method for frustrated Ising antiferromagnets on periodic Kagome graphs with up to 36 spins, using the ibm_kingston quantum processor. Despite substantial circuit depth and hardware noise, the reconstructed spectra retain their dominant features, and the calculated heat capacities reproduce the main temperature dependence of the exact results.   Keywords: partition function, imaginary temperature, Ising model, heat capacity, ancilla qubit, quantum computing.
summary: This work proposes a hybrid quantum-classical method to determine the energy spectrum and thermodynamic properties of spin systems by measuring the partition function using a single ancilla qubit. The technique leverages the inverse DFT to reconstruct degeneracies, showing that while hardware noise limits perfect spectral reconstruction, the overall thermodynamic behavior remains reliably measurable. This provides a pathway to simulate complex quantum materials on near-term quantum hardware.
main_problem: The paper aims to reconstruct the energy-level degeneracies and calculate the thermodynamic properties of complex spin systems.
main_result: The hybrid quantum-classical method successfully recovers the overall temperature dependence of thermodynamic quantities like heat capacity, even when hardware noise limits the exact reconstruction of individual energy degeneracies.
method: It uses a single ancilla qubit to measure the complex partition function $Z(it)$ at imaginary inverse temperatures, followed by an inverse Discrete Fourier Transform (DFT) to estimate the spectral weights.
model_or_system: The study focuses on spin systems governed by an Ising-type Hamiltonian, benchmarked on frustrated antiferromagnets on periodic Kagome graphs (up to 36 spins).
key_observables: Partition function $Z( eta)$, energy-level degeneracies ($g_k$), and heat capacity $C( eta)$.
important_parameters: Imaginary inverse temperature ($ eta = it$), system size ($N=36$), and the spectral spacing ($\Delta E$).
main_assumptions: The DFT reconstruction is exact only in the absence of noise, and the results rely on post-processing steps like thresholding and renormalization to enforce physical constraints.
figures_summary: Figures compare ancilla expectation values, reconstructed spectral weights, and calculated heat capacities against exact theoretical results for small and large Kagome clusters.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the thermodynamic link to the partition function, detailing the quantum protocol using the ancilla qubit, and finally applying the DFT reconstruction technique to calculate thermodynamic observables for increasingly large spin systems.
why_interesting: It demonstrates a powerful quantum measurement technique to probe bulk thermodynamic properties of interacting quantum many-body systems, which is a core problem in condensed matter theory.
